creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Owner's choice, 2026-11-08: direction B's Needs you strip, on top of direction A's list, and foldable (Lectern page muster-ui-redesign, section "Chosen").

The strip has one card per agent that wants the person: blocked, stuck, finished and unseen, or holding messages for them. Each card shows the callsign, the chord, the state and how long it has held, and for a message the start of its text. Folded, the strip is one line with each card's state icon. It is absent while nothing needs anyone.

An agent in the strip keeps its row in the list below, so the list never reorders. What a blocked agent asked needs a fact no field carries yet, which is its own card; until then a blocked card can show the subtitle its row already has.

The core should decide what is in the strip and in what order, as it decides the roster, and in the same order focus_asking walks, so the chord and the strip agree and `muster window` can say the same.

Fencil decision needs-you-strip (owner-decided).

## Plan (reviewed 2026-11-08)

From the plan for the redesign, step 3; the parent card a_2wKW8eBfM has its overall shape, order and checks.

The core already ranks everything asking for the person: `Attention::asking()` in
`crates/muster-core/src/attention.rs` sorts by alert (blocked, stuck, message, notified, done) and
then by an ordering counter for who asked first. The shell sees only its head (`AskingChanged`,
`FocusAsking`).

- The strip is exactly `Attention::asking()`. One list means the strip, `focus_asking` and the
  banners never disagree about who is waiting. It follows that list's rules: a quiet pane is not in
  it, nor is a pane the focused window is showing, nor anything on an unreachable machine.
- New per-window event `AskingListChanged { repeated AskingEntry entries }`. An entry carries the
  asker (a pane key or a group key), the alert, `since_ms`, and for a group a `preview`. It carries
  no labels or counts: the shell draws those from the roster, `PaneStateChanged` and
  `GroupsChanged`, which it already joins by key for every row.
- `since_ms` for a state alert (blocked, stuck, done) is the pane's own `since_ms` from its state
  record, so a window that starts with a pane already blocked shows how long it has really waited.
  For a program's notification and for a group, it is when the core raised the alert, recorded in
  `Raised` beside the ordering counter: a notification does not change the pane's state, so a shell
  idle for a day that posts one has waited seconds, not a day.
- A group's `preview` is the start of the latest message for the human, fetched from the group's
  log through the path `session::human_noticed` uses for banners (`banners::fetch`), not from
  `HumanNotice.said`, which only Muster's own messages fill. It is fetched whether or not
  notifications are on, and independently of the banner stack, so a banner whose draft pins an older
  message does not hold back the preview.
- The core compares whole entries, not only their order, and emits when any entry changes: a second
  message to the same group updates its preview without moving it.
- `muster window --json` gains the same ordered list, so an agent sees what the person sees
  (AGENTS.md, "AI-native surface").
- `docs/cli/agents.md` describes `focus --asking` as "blocked, then notification, then done", which
  is already stale; it is corrected to the real order with this step.
- What a blocked agent is asking stays out of this step (card `a_2wKWAO18V`); until it lands, a
  blocked card shows the pane's subtitle.
- Tests (conformance and seam): the list's order across alerts and arrival; a second message to the
  same group; a renamed asking pane redrawn without a new list; a window started with a pane already
  blocked; a long-idle shell posting a notification; a banner pinned to an older message beside a
  newer preview.
title: A foldable Needs you strip at the top of the agent list
